                    ### Question
                    Which of the following statements is correct with respect to hepatic hemangiomas?

                    ### Options
                    opa. They can be associated with the KasabachMerritt syndrome (thrombocytopenia and consumption coagulopathy), especially giant hemangiomas.
opb. Surgical exeresis should be indicated from the moment it is diagnosed if its diameter is greater than 3 cm.
opc. Percutaneous embolization is the most recommended therapeutic option for this type of tumor.
opd. The best method for its diagnostic confirmation is percutaneous biopsy of the liver lesion.
ope. Hepatic MRI does not usually offer much help for its diagnostic characterization.

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Hepatic hemangiomas are benign vascular tumors that are usually asymptomatic and do not require surgical intervention unless they cause symptoms or complications. Giant hemangiomas can be associated with Kasabach-Merritt syndrome, which leads to thrombocytopenia and consumption coagulopathy. Surgical resection is not routinely indicated based solely on size (greater than 3 cm) without symptoms. Percutaneous embolization is not the first-line treatment; surgical resection is preferred for symptomatic cases. Biopsy is generally unnecessary due to the characteristic imaging features of hemangiomas, which can be effectively diagnosed through MRI. MRI is valuable for differentiating hemangiomas from other liver lesions, confirming its role in diagnostic characterization.
